title: Inference cost, stability, and model deprecation roadmap
next_steps: Redwood to share month-to-date token and embedding cost breakouts (Ava) by 2026-03-12
Run model retirement impact benchmark on staging for top-3 endpoints (Samir) by 2026-03-19
Customer to confirm internal deprecation policy and list of models to retire (Marco) by 2026-03-18
Schedule follow-up QBR in 6 weeks to review pilot results (Ruth/Zephyr)
action_items: Ava Martinez: Export token-level bill and annotate heavy routes — due 2026-03-12
Samir Patel: Run 95th percentile latency + cost benchmarks for quantized variants — due 2026-03-19
Marco Ruiz: Provide model retirement candidate list and traffic share per endpoint — due 2026-03-18
Priya Desai: Share SLOs and current incident runbook excerpts for inference services — due 2026-03-15
header: Date: 2026-03-08 16:30 UTC; Duration: 58m; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes; Redwood attendees: Ava, Samir, Ruth; Zephyr attendees: Lina, Marco, Priya, Omar, Jules
summary: Quarterly health checkpoint focused on balancing cost reductions with reliability during planned model deprecations and rollout of cheaper quantized variants. Agreed to run targeted benchmarks and share annotated cost breakouts. Customer will confirm retirement candidates and timelines.
transcript:
00:00 Ava (Redwood AE): alright everyone uh thanks for joining, we've got about an hour, agenda is cost, stability, and the model deprecation plan. quick intros?
00:12 Lina (Zephyr CTO): Lina here, hi all. we want to understand how retiring old models will affect latency and cost, also finance on the call.
00:20 Omar (Finance): Omar — quick question up front, how much runway would we get if we deprecate three older models we no longer train?
00:30 Ava: good — we'll walk through numbers. Samir will show the benchmark plan and Ruth will cover operational impact.
00:36 Samir (Redwood SE): hi, i'll jump into perf notes, but first, initial ask — Marco, do you have list of endpoints you consider candidates?
00:45 Marco (Head of ML): yes, we have three — summarize-norm, intent-v1, and rerank-lite. traffic is about 18% of total tokens across the account, but intent-v1 is heavy on short requests.
00:58 Priya (SRE): latency sensitivity differs; intent-v1 is used in sync UI flows so p95 matters.
01:10 Ava: on costs — top-level: embeddings and long-form generation drive ~62% of token spend, but those three models are disproportionately used in routing and intermediate reranks. I'll share a breakdown after the call.
01:24 Omar: rough numbers we got last month looked like a 12% delta if we moved everything to quantized variants, is that accurate?
01:31 Samir: 12% across the whole bill seems plausible but depends on batching and prefix reuse. the model-level delta can be much higher for the older FP16 variants. quantized LLMs drop per-token GPU cost substantially, but sometimes they increase latency by a few ms.
01:50 Jules (PM): curious — what about the cost of extra engineering to switch models? e.g., changes in prompts, post-processing, evaluation.
02:01 Ruth (CSM): good point — we should include an operational overhead estimate. i'll draft a checklist for model retirement playbook.
02:10 Ava: ok let's sketch a two-track approach: non-live pilot on staging for safety and perf, and a controlled canary on hosted for low-traffic routes.
02:21 Marco: staging performance is representative for latency but not for real user routing. we need to test fallback paths in canary.
02:30 Samir: agreed. for staging we'll run three tests: steady-state traffic replay, burst stress, and long-sequence generation. playback will use KV cache emulation but watch out — sometimes the transcriber (laugh) i mean the traffic simulator mis-handles KV caching so we need to validate.
02:55 Priya: on SLOs, our current p95 is 220ms for intent-v1, p99 480ms. if a quantized variant pushes p95 above 300ms that's a concern.
03:12 Samir: understood, we'll collect p50/p95/p99 and tail variance, and also token-per-second throughput.
03:20 Lina: what about security? we have compliance checks for decommissioning models, we need audit trail that proves inference outputs for N days were generated by model X before retire.
03:30 Ruth: Redwood supports model-level audit logs and request attribution in the console, we can export audit logs and tie them to your retention policy.
03:40 Omar: encryption — are keys rotated automatically? if we move to private deployment later, KMS integration matters.
03:47 Ava: yes, KMS/HSM integration is available for Private; hosted has envelope encryption and rotation schedule, i'll attach SOC2 / security deck.
03:57 Marco: one subtlety — the rerank-lite model is used inside a batch microservice that aggregates results. it expects consistent tokenization and ordering. any change in logits could change downstream ranking drastically.
04:12 Samir: we'll include delta-tests for ranking drift and tuning knobs like temperature and top-k adjustments. for rerank variants we recommend a short A/B on 1% of traffic.
04:25 Jules: can we get an expected revenue impact if ranking drifts? that's hard but product needs estimate.
04:33 Omar: finance wants conservative numbers — a small drop in conversion is worse than a small cost saving.
04:40 Ava: that's why pilot + canary + rollback policy. Redwood's rollout supports canary percentage and automatic fallback to the previous model on error rate or p95 regression.
04:55 Priya: we also need playbooks for incident ops — who paginates, and runbook steps.
05:02 Ruth: i'll share the runbook template and we can align runbook owners.
05:10 Marco: what's the expected timeline to fully deprecate the three models?
05:16 Ava: tentative 8-10 weeks from pilot start: 1) collect candidate list and traffic map (week 1), 2) staging benchmarks and tuning (weeks 2-3), 3) small canary and user-facing metrics (weeks 4-6), 4) roll forward + monitor and final cutover (week 8-10).
05:34 Lina: that works if we can keep tight observable dashboards.
05:40 Samir: dashboarding — we'll provide prebuilt dashboards for p50/p95/p99, cost-per-1k-tokens, and rollout signals including error rates and quality regressions from your eval set.
05:56 Marco: eval set — we'll need guidance on selecting prompts that matter. our rerank edge-cases live in the long tail, not in the top 100 prompts.
06:06 Samir: capture static prompt corpora and live-sampled prompts. we will recommend both.
06:14 Omar: back to costs: can you show how autoscaling/burst affects monthly bill? we saw spikes last holiday and the committed pool didn't cover burst.
06:25 Ava: yes — dedicated pools reduce per-token cost when committed, but if you burst beyond reserved capacity, burst pricing applies. we'll annotate your last three spikes and show how different reserved capacity levels change unit cost.
06:40 Priya: note: network egress to private deployments adds measurable cost vs hosted. keep that in mind for private migration.
06:48 Ava: good call, include network, storage for KV cache, and cross-region replication in the cost model.
06:55 Lina: are there quick wins to save cost now without affecting UX?
07:00 Samir: yes — intelligent caching/prefix reuse improvements and route-level batching. also identify long context sessions where you can truncate historical context safely. that can cut tokens by 8-15% for some features.
07:12 Marco: are those changes easy on our side? the client lib has hooks?
07:18 Samir: yes, Redwood SDK supports prefix caching and you can opt in per route; we can ship config suggestions.
07:26 Jules: from product side we can prioritize routes with highest token-per-conversion ratio.
07:33 Ruth: i'll run a route-priority matrix and share.
07:40 Ava: ok let's talk specific benchmark plan — Samir?
07:44 Samir: for each candidate model: 1) cost-per-1k tokens at 16 and 8-bit quantized profiles, 2) p50/p95/p99 latency under batching profiles (1, 4, 8) and different sequence lengths, 3) regression eval on provided prompt sets, 4) canary plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with automated rollback. we'll provide a template spreadsheet for results.
08:10 Marco: templates please. also include a column for downstream ranking delta.
08:15 Samir: yes.
08:18 Priya: what about canary PBIs — how do we assert business-level KPIs? we need KPI threshold mapping.
08:26 Ava: map model-level metrics to product KPI buckets: latency, error-rate, ranking delta, and conversion delta if available. we'll help set conservative thresholds.
08:36 Lina: any regulatory issues about model deprecation? we are in healthcare-adjacent workflows, need records.
08:44 Ruth: keep an immutable audit export for the retired window; Redwood can provide exports for the retention window. also we log config changes.
08:55 Marco: curious on long-term strategy — do you recommend pivoting more traffic to hosted optimized models vs dedicated pools?
09:03 Samir: depends — high-volume, predictable workloads are best on Dedicated for unit economics. unpredictable or low-volume is fine on Hosted. also routing policy can split by cost tier.
09:17 Omar: what delta should we budget to avoid surprise bills during migration?
09:21 Ava: recommend a 15% contingency in the first 30 days and a weekly review for the first month. we'll produce a forecast with bands.
09:33 Jules: can you show sample rollback metrics? e.g. how quickly we can detect a regression and cut traffic back.
09:40 Samir: detection within 5 minutes for automated metrics, rollback enforced within minutes depending on traffic ramp. manual confirmation for business KPIs will be slower.
09:52 Priya: how will alerts surface? via webhooks to our PagerDuty?
09:56 Ruth: yes — Redwood supports PagerDuty and webhook alerts for thresholds.
10:02 Lina: let's talk about costs of keeping old models for compliance, is cold storage an option?
10:09 Ava: you can snapshot model artifacts to cold storage, keep logs for required retention, but serving requires model in active pool. we can archive weights and metadata and restore on demand, but restore time is not instant.
10:22 Marco: how long to restore?
10:24 Samir: depends on size and provisioning, typically 30-90 minutes for a full-sized model on GPU; smaller quantized variants faster.
10:34 Lina: that may be acceptable, we just need a documented SLA for retrieval.
10:40 Ruth: we'll include restore time guidance and recommended retention lifecycle.
10:46 Ava: quick check — are there any blockers from security or finance to proceed with pilot?
10:51 Omar: finance wants clearer expected savings and contingency plan, but no Blocker.
10:55 Priya: security needs the audit export and KMS notes, not a blocker.
11:02 Marco: engineering capacity is limited in two weeks, so timeline should take that into account.
11:07 Ava: noted — we'll calendar milestones assuming a resource ramp.
11:12 Lina: ok let's recap next steps.
11:15 Ava: recap: Redwood will share annotated cost workbook and dashboard templates (Ava), Samir will do staging benchmark plan and spreadsheet and then run quantized tests on staging (Samir), Ruth will share deprecation/runbook templates (Ruth), Marco will provide final candidate list/traffic share (Marco).
11:30 Lina: thanks, if we can get the cost breakout by Friday that helps budgeting.
11:35 Ava: we'll get it out by 2026-03-12.
11:39 Ruth: i'll set a follow-up QBR for 6 weeks and propose calendar times.
11:45 Omar: please also include a conservative delta to revenue modeling.
11:49 Ava: noted. thanks everyone.
11:55 End of recording: final misc chat about follow-up docs and who will own benchmarks.
